**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues

body:
Next step: figure out whether this is safe to default
* When does docker runtime supports it
* When does containerd supports it out of the box
* How about other registry 
* What about podman

I checked the runtimes and downstream importers. Docker Engine 23 supports normal zstd pulls without the containerd image store; the classic-store tests passed on 23.0.6/29.1.3 and failed on 20.10.24. Containerd 1.5 has a built-in decoder, and Podman 1.6.2 includes it through containers/image. Those last two are source/dependency checks, not new runtime tests. Podman's gzip push default doesn't prevent it from pulling zstd. [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/engine/release-notes/23.0/), [containerd](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/v1.5.0/archive/compression/compression.go), [Podman dependencies](https://github.com/containers/podman/blob/v1.6.2/go.mod), [containers/image decoder](https://github.com/containers/image/blob/v4.0.0/pkg/compression/compression.go).

The two gotchas I found are Enroot and SOCI. Enroot 3.5's actual download/cache function fails to produce the right tar from zstd input; I reproduced that with a small fixture and gzip controls. Enroot 4.0 adds zstd, but 4.2 fixes mixed-compression images, which matters when someone adds a gzip layer to our image. Pyxis uses that importer too. SOCI v0.15.0 cannot build zstd lazy-loading indexes, even though ordinary containerd unpack supports the image. [Enroot 4.0](https://github.com/NVIDIA/enroot/releases/tag/v4.0.0), [mixed-layer fix in 4.2](https://github.com/NVIDIA/enroot/releases/tag/v4.2.0), [SOCI source](https://github.com/awslabs/soci-snapshotter/blob/v0.15.0/ztoc/compression/zinfo.go).

Hub delivery and full vLLM serving already passed. I also checked the copy/build/archive paths: an added layer can create a mixed-compression image, and a mirror can re-encode it, so signing/scanning needs to cover the final delivered digest. Other OCI registries are expected to work, but I haven't run a separate cloud matrix.

I'd keep this opt-in for now. A zstd default looks reasonable if we document the supported runtime/importer versions and keep an easy-to-find gzip compatibility tag, including for SOCI users. Without that, changing the existing tag would break some downstream workflows.

- Your branch must contain every commit currently on its upstream target branch. Merge or rebase onto the latest target branch, then rerun the command. Append `--allow-stale` to a run command to test an outdated branch at your own risk.
- `/ci retry` retries failed jobs in the CI build for the current PR head. If the current head has no CI build, it starts a new CI build for the current head containing only jobs that failed in the latest earlier CI build for this PR.
- `/amd-ci retry` retries failed jobs in AMD CI for the current PR head. Use `/amd-ci run` when the current head has no AMD CI build.
- `/ci cancel` cancels scheduled or running CI builds for this PR branch; `/amd-ci cancel` does the same for AMD CI only.
